newsitem.title: USA: U.S. agency freezes housing money of Camden, N.J..
newsitem.headline: U.S. agency freezes housing money of Camden, N.J..

text.p: U.S. Housing and Urban Development officials have frozen the spending power of the Camden, New Jersey, housing authority, a newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The Philadelphia Inquirer said it was the last step to prepare for a federal takeover of the agency.
The seven-member housing authority board in New Jersey's poorest city scheduled a meeting for Friday, when it will be asked to turn over its assets to federal authorities, the newspaper said.
The move ends a three-year struggle that has seen a nearly total turnover in the local authority's leadership, and a much longer pattern of neglect, HUD officials said.
In 1996 tenant members were added to the board.

The primary issue was the board's failure to implement a plan to refurbish a collapsing housing project called McGuire Gardens, even though it has had a $42 million federal grant for three years. Many of the 369 units were boarded up and abandoned, and the plan to build new retail space, rebuild a community centre and day-care centre was never implemented.
